{{About|shrinking topological spaces|shrinking civic spaces|civic space#Violations{{!}}Civic space}}

In [[mathematics]], in the field of [[topology]], a [[topological space]] is said to have the '''shrinking property'''<ref name="egt"/> or to be a '''shrinking space''' if every [[open cover]] admits a shrinking. A ''shrinking'' of an open cover is another open cover indexed by the same indexing set, with the property that the closure of each open set in the shrinking lies inside the corresponding original open set.<ref name="egt">{{citation|title=Encyclopedia of General Topology|first1=K. P.|last1=Hart|first2=Jun-iti|last2=Nagata|first3=J. E.|last3=Vaughan|publisher=[[Elsevier]]|year=2003|isbn=9780080530864|page=199|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=JWyoCRkLFAkC&pg=PA199}}.</ref>

== Properties ==

The following facts are known about shrinking spaces:

* Every shrinking space is [[normal space|normal]].<ref name="egt"/>
* Every shrinking space is [[countably paracompact]].<ref name="egt"/>
* In a [[normal space]], every locally finite, and in fact, every point-finite open cover admits a shrinking.<ref name="egt"/>
* Thus, every normal [[metacompact space]] is a shrinking space. In particular, every Hausdorff [[paracompact space]] is a shrinking space.<ref name="egt"/>

These facts are particularly important because shrinking of open covers is a common technique in the theory of [[differential manifold]]s and while constructing functions using a [[partition of unity]].
